blocks.body: Sewer rodding clears a blocked main line with a long, flexible steel cable fed through a cleanout access point. A cutting head on the end breaks through roots, grease, and debris and pushes the blockage toward the street connection, restoring flow through the pipe. It's the standard first fix for a clogged or backed-up sewer line. For most homes, it's the only fix needed.

img.alt: Diagram showing a rodding cable fed through a cleanout access point into the main sewer line, with a cutting head clearing the blockage toward the street connection

blocks.h2: What Blocks Main Lines in Geneva
blocks.intro: From historic homes to new subdivisions, we clear every kind of main line clog in Geneva.

items.body: Older lines near the river let roots in at every joint, and they grow into mats.
Original cast iron inside older homes builds rust scale that catches debris.

items.h3: Wipes and Grease in Newer Homes
items.body: In 1990s and 2000s homes, most clogs come from what goes down the drain.
Fast-returning roots call for [hydro jetting](/geneva/hydro-jetting). Damage calls for a [sewer repair](/geneva/sewer-repair).

steps.body: Floors protected, work done from the cleanout.
Line cleared to the main, then inspected so you see the cause.
Agreed before we start. Options priced if we find damage.

blocks.h2: Sewer Rodding Questions From Geneva Homeowners

items.q: How do I know it's the main line?
items.preview: The floor drain or several fixtures are affected.
items.answer: When the floor drain backs up or several fixtures are slow or gurgling, the clog is in the main line rather than one fixture.

items.q: How often should an older Geneva home be rodded?
items.preview: Once a year if roots are present.
items.answer: If roots have blocked the line before, once a year is typical, ideally in late winter or early spring.

items.q: Will rodding damage an old clay pipe?
items.preview: Not when done right. The camera shows its condition.
items.answer: Not with the right cutting head. If the pipe is already broken, the camera will show it and we'll stop and explain.

items.preview: Usually in the basement or just outside.
items.answer: In most homes, it's in the basement near where the line leaves, or in the yard by the foundation. Some older homes don't have one, and adding one makes future work easier.

items.q: How much does sewer rodding cost in Geneva?
items.preview: It depends on access and the clog. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on where the cleanout is, the length of the line and what's blocking it. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
